reason: The cited lines show the tool validates a user-supplied path, recursively reads directories with fs.readdir, matches path names with minimatch, and returns full matching host filesystem paths. That supports SECRET because host filesystem paths/directory entries from allowed directories are returned into the agent context. The lines do not show arbitrary code execution, network/file writes, or delivery to an attacker-readable external destination, so HOSTEXEC and SINK are not supported. Although filenames can sometimes be attacker-controlled, these lines alone do not establish attacker control over the searched filesystem contents, so UNTRUSTED is insufficient.
